boundary_decision.rationale: The root is a versioned return-and-refund case aggregate. Order, fulfilment, party, item, shipment, inventory, entitlement, invoice, credit note, payment, warranty, recall, dispute, waste and records remain external masters.

decisions.rationale: One case can bind request, decision, reverse movement, inspection, adjustment and payment evidence without owning the referenced commercial, physical, financial or legal masters.
The unified registry supplies a parent hint but the frozen relation ledger has no settled edge. It is retained as a non-canonical reference and grants no containment or cascade authority.
A request is not entitlement and an eligibility assessment is not authorization. Each assertion keeps rule version, scope, evidence, authority, event time and knowledge time.

decisions.concept: Goods, service, digital and non-return refund profiles
decisions.rationale: The aggregate can express these profiles, but no one movement, inspection, access-revocation or refund path is made universal across them.
Subject identity, quantity, condition, custody and receipt are local bindings and observations; shipment, package, inventory, location and waste execution remain external.
Receipt, inspection, return acceptance and disposition are not equivalent, and restock, repair, quarantine, recycle, destroy or access-revoke execution remains in authoritative sibling systems.
Price, tax, fee, discount, deposit, deduction, allocation, currency and rounding inputs support an auditable obligation, but the case does not issue accounting records or move funds.

decisions.concept: Credit, refund instruction, execution and settlement
decisions.rationale: A credit note is not a payment, a payment instruction is not execution, execution is not settlement, and settlement does not prove receipt by the intended beneficiary without evidence.
These lifecycles can create, constrain or contest a return/refund case but remain independently authoritative and cannot be closed by this aggregate.
CISG and EU rules are scoped legal profiles, while IFRS describes accounting treatment rather than individual entitlement. None is presented as universal law.
UBL, UN/EDIFACT, ISO 20022, EU, IFRS, EPCIS, CBV, Schema.org, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI cover different facets and never replace the canonical case aggregate.

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet and one bounded Grok attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex separately audited the frozen validated result and comparison without new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

deferred_research: Canonically adjudicate the WM-ECO-024 parent signal and register return/refund relations to order, fulfilment, shipment, inventory, invoice, payment, warranty, recall, chargeback, dispute and waste models.
Create consumer, business, marketplace, subscription, travel, digital, regulated-goods, hazardous-material and cross-border return profiles.
Conformance-test return, receipt, inspection, disposition, adjustment, payment and projection mappings against concrete implementations.
Validate organization-specific eligibility, evidence, fraud, tax, accounting, payment-route, safety, privacy, retention and exception policies.
Obtain authorized legal, consumer, finance, tax, logistics, product-safety and records review before jurisdiction-specific claims.
Obtain independent external research review before promotion beyond reviewable-draft assurance.
publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok attempt for WM-ECO-025 each timed out after 120 seconds; no external result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-ECO-024 is only a provisional parent signal and the frozen relation ledger contains no settled WM-ECO-025 edge.

Boundary hold: return request, eligibility, authorization, reverse shipment, receipt, inspection, disposition, refund obligation, credit note, payment return or reversal, chargeback and dispute retain separate identities.
Profile hold: goods, services, digital content, access, consumer, business, marketplace, subscription, travel and regulated-sector cases require separate conformance profiles.

Quantity and condition hold: every requested, authorized, handed-over, received, inspected, accepted and dispositioned value requires subject, unit, lot or serial, source, method, time and uncertainty.
Financial hold: price, tax, fee, discount, deposit, deduction, allocation, currency and rounding require authoritative invoice, tax, accounting and payment references.

State-axis hold: request, eligibility, authorization, custody, receipt, inspection, disposition, credit, instruction, execution, settlement, customer receipt and closure states and clocks must not collapse.

Authority hold: legal eligibility, return authorization, custody, condition judgment, physical disposition, accounting adjustment, refund execution, disclosure and destruction require delegated authority.
Jurisdiction hold: CISG and EU consumer, goods, digital and product-safety rules are scoped profiles; national, sector, tax, payment-scheme and contract rules need validation.
Source-access hold: UNECE pages were indexed but direct automated access was publisher-blocked, and the official IFRS issued-standard document redirected to sign-in.
Interoperability hold: every UBL, UN/EDIFACT, ISO 20022, EU, IFRS, EPCIS, CBV, Schema.org, RFC, PROV, DQV, ODRL and OpenAPI projection needs release pins, conformance evidence and loss declarations.
Privacy hold: party, address, account, payment, item, serial, condition, fraud, dispute and evidence data require purpose-bound access, minimization and retention controls.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
